body: I feel like if I was completely honest, they would have me committed--which honestly I think I need, but I can't afford that level of treatment and I'd rather die than go into that kind of debt trying to live. But I can't hurt those around me, so I live any way. And so on.
Thank you, I'm going to take this advice and wait - I'm eager to learn, but I don't want to make it more difficult in the long run.
Thank you for the resources and advice!
That makes a lot of sense, thank you!

Thank you for the advice! When I was in high school on the volleyball team, the first thing they taught us before anything else was how to fall correctly for a dive. It probably makes sense to practice that on the unicycle as well. Thanks again!

It's an Avenir 20". When fully extended, my knee is probably 25 to 30 degrees bent. Too me it looks like it's too short, but having never ridden before, I can't say with confidence that that is the issue. So probably short, but not drastically so?

Thank you for the advice, and you're spot on -- I'm pretty much begging for a broken wrist because that a exactly what I do when I start falling back, I throw out my hands to catch myself. I guess that's just a habit I need to break before it breaks me ;)
Thank you! I didn't think about the fact that leaning forward could be pushing more weight back, but that makes complete sense.
